the following aspects: * The prognostic value of the Swan-Ganz technique in the early stage of multiple trauma patients.
the early prediction of a fatal outcome in patients with severe injuries by means of the Swan-Ganz technique.
the early detection of metabolic and haemodynamic patterns, which are predictive for a favourable outcome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the haemodynamic pattern in the early stage of multiple trauma is characterised by a high cardiac index, a high pulmonary artery pressure and a high right ventricular stroke index.
a high cardiac output, a low oxygen availability, and a high oxygen extraction are the best prognostic factors in the first 2 h after trauma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic and haemodynamic values of multiple trauma patients permit an early prediction as to whether a patient is going to survive.
a combination of haemodynamic, respiratory and metabolic values at the very beginning can provide a good prognosis for survival in patients with severe trauma.

there are significant differences in the haemodynamic and the metabolic parameters between the survivors and non-surviors.
the early use of Swan-Ganz catheters is of great value for prognosis in severe trauma patients, especially when the metabolic parameters are taken into account.
